comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C9, C89, C138 regarding the novelty and importance of the first sex-specific arterial myocyte model. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED with strong affirmation from all reviewers.

Perfect agreement on claims C131-C134 regarding clinical relevance and sex-specific drug responses. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers accepting the translational value without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C135-C137 regarding model limitations. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers accepting the stated limitations as appropriate and viewing them as opportunities for future expansion.

Strong agreement on claims C4, C5, C26, C27, C36, C37, C91, C92 regarding sex-specific differences in L-type Ca2+ and KV channels. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED with careful experimental validation. Peer review also includes C33, C90 which OpenEval grouped separately.

Agreement on experimental measurements (C30-C32) with appropriate sample sizes and statistical analysis. Both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer review groups C2, C38 together while OpenEval separates them, but both affirm the findings.

Agreement on claims C2, C38 regarding comparable KV1.5 properties between sexes. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats this separately while peer review groups it with other experimental findings.

Agreement on claims C3, C62, C63, C96 regarding KV1.5 dominance in males. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. Peer review also includes C6, C64, C65, C97 (KV2.1 in females) as part of the same major finding, while OpenEval separates these.

Agreement on claims C6, C64, C97 regarding KV2.1 dominance in females. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. Peer review groups this with C3 findings as a unified discovery, while OpenEval treats them separately.

Agreement on claims C40-C45 regarding BKCa channel properties and modeling. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. Peer review specifically praises the stochastic modeling approach as 'particularly clever.'

Agreement on claims C48-C54 regarding experimental observations of sex-specific membrane potential oscillations. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED with strong experimental-computational agreement. Peer review also includes C80-C83 (tissue model), while OpenEval separates these.

Agreement on claims C80-C83 regarding 1D tissue model predictions and smoothing effects. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. Peer review groups this with membrane potential oscillations, while OpenEval treats them separately.

Agreement on claims C66-C70, C115-C116 regarding Ca2+ handling and cellular excitability predictions. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED as a major finding linking membrane potential to Ca2+ dynamics.

Agreement on claims C7, C110-C114, C140 regarding small channel numbers controlling physiological function. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. Peer review groups this with broader Ca2+ handling findings, while OpenEval emphasizes the specific quantitative predictions.

Divergence in evaluation type: OpenEval marks claims C58-C60, C108 as UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanism ('most likely due to Na+-permeable TRP channels'), while peer reviewers find the mechanistic predictions SUPPORTED and accept the sensitivity analysis results without expressing uncertainty.

Agreement on claims C100-C106 regarding mechanistic predictions of oscillatory behavior. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers affirming the model's value for mechanistic understanding.

Agreement on claims C8, C28, C29, C84-C88, C130 regarding Ca2+ channel blocker sensitivity predictions. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED as a key finding with experimental validation. Peer review also includes C73-C76, C78, C129, C141.

Agreement on claims C73-C78 regarding nifedipine effects and sex-specific Ca2+ channel blocker responses. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. Peer review groups this with broader drug sensitivity findings, while OpenEval treats model predictions separately.
Agreement on claims C84-C85 regarding experimental validation of model predictions. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED with strong experimental-computational agreement.

Agreement on claims C119-C120 regarding stochastic effects and channel variability. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers praising the stochastic modeling approach. Peer review also includes C128.

OpenEval evaluated claims C11-C22 (background literature on arterial myocyte mechanisms) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background context.
